subject.title: Device identity generation should not depend on browser Secure Context — breaks HTTP reverse-proxy deployments

question: Should OpenClaw allow persistent Control UI browser device identity to be generated and used in non-localhost plain-HTTP contexts?
rationale: Current docs intentionally require HTTPS or localhost for browser device identity, and changing that behavior would alter the auth boundary for operator access in tamperable browser transports.

options.title: Keep secure-context default
options.body: Continue rejecting remote plain-HTTP browser device identity and focus on clearer HTTPS, trusted-proxy, Tailscale, SSH tunnel, and break-glass guidance.

options.title: Design an explicit opt-in
options.body: Add remote plain-HTTP device identity only behind a clear, audited operator opt-in with docs and tests for upgrade, warning, and threat-model behavior.

options.title: Allow by default
options.body: Remove the WebCrypto/secure-context dependency and always attempt browser identity generation, accepting the plaintext transport threat-model change.

recommendation.title: Design an explicit opt-in
recommendation.body: Add remote plain-HTTP device identity only behind a clear, audited operator opt-in with docs and tests for upgrade, warning, and threat-model behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The current secure Control UI auth boundary and recent current-path ownership both trace most strongly to steipete/Peter Steinberger history.
